problems.title: Incorrect leading normalization in Theorem3
problems.source_claim: Theorem3 states the exact Bessel series M_k(y)=alpha*sqrt(y)*sum_{d,s>=1}Q(d)J_{k-1}(4*pi*s*sqrt(y)/d)/s, followed by the leading coefficient alpha*(-1)^(k/2-1)*sqrt(2/pi) multiplying y^(1/4) F(sqrt(y)).
assumptions: Fixed even integer k>=2; y>0 and y tends to infinity.
alpha has the same positive normalization in both displays; J_nu is the standard Bessel function.
Q(d)>=0,Q(1)=1,Q(d)=O(d^-2), since every local factor is positive and product_p p^4/A_p converges.

decisive_check.type: analytic proof recovered and checked against cited source; no new numerical run
decisive_check.uniform_remainder: Split d<=sT and d>sT. In first range the summed asymptotic remainder is O_k(T^-1/2 sum_s s^-5/2 sum_{d<=sT}d^-1/2)=O_k(1). In second range bounded J on[0,4*pi] gives O_k(T sum_s s^-1 sum_{d>sT}d^-2)=O_k(1), and the removed leading tail is O(T^1/2 sum_s s^-3/2 sum_{d>sT}d^-3/2)=O(1).
decisive_check.counterexample_parameters: k=2, T_n=n!, y_n=(n!)^2. All stated domain conditions are satisfied.
decisive_check.nonvanishing: B=zeta(3/2)*sum_d Q(d)*sqrt(d) is finite and positive. Absolute convergence and eventual d|n! give F(n!)->-B/sqrt(2).
decisive_check.discrepancy: Leading coefficients differ by factor2*sqrt(pi); the difference is order y^(1/4) along this sequence, not O(1).

counterevidence: Theorem statement has the correct parity phase; the proof's (-1)^(k/2) is a separate sign inconsistency.
The primary rendered pages and companion TeX agree locally, excluding an OCR-only explanation.
A shared rescaling of alpha cannot reconcile the two stated expressions while retaining their exact Bessel argument and standard normalization.
The printed O(min(z^-3/2,1)) expression cannot uniformly describe the error near zero; the split-range proof bypasses that problem.
problems.core_dependency: Theorem3 is a principal asymptotic description of the murmurations density. A wrong leading asymptotic is a core mathematical defect under the frozen severity criterion even though it has a short repair.
problems.impact_boundary: The growth order y^(1/4), universal oscillatory series and qualitative parity dependence survive; no failure of the original modular-form correlation or computational sign-change conclusion is inferred.

correction.verification: Analytically verified within the exact Bessel-representation basis; no changed domain assumptions.

problems.title: Impossible RH remainder in Lemma7.3, known issue reproduced

source_locator.claim: Lemma7.3 and Section7.3 dependency in proof of Theorem6

problems.source_claim: Assuming RH, sum_{d<=T}Q(d)=L-Delta/T+R(T) with R(T)<<_epsilon T^(-2+epsilon). Its proof shifts a Perron contour to Re(s)=-2+epsilon and counts only poles0,-1.
assumptions: RH for the Riemann zeta function, exactly as in the source lemma.
The same nonnegative Q(d) and A_p as Problem1.
Choose any nontrivial zeta zero rho=1/2+i*gamma; simplicity is not required.
For the contradiction choose a fixed0<epsilon<1/4.
Theorem6 additionally takes fixed c>1 and even k>=6; its sharp-average conclusion is distinguished from the defective proof.

decisive_check.local_identity: Multiplying a local H factor by 1+p^(-s-2) yields1+p^(2-s)/A_p.
decisive_check.holomorphy: H is locally uniformly absolutely convergent and holomorphic for Re(s)>-2; each denominator is nonzero there.
decisive_check.genuine_pole: At s0=(rho-4)/2=-7/4+i*gamma/2, zeta(2s0+4)=0 while zeta(s0+2)=zeta(rho/2)!=0 under RH. Any vanishing local H factor would force A_p^4=p^15, impossible because A_p=1 mod p. Thus H(s0)!=0 and L has a nonremovable pole, regardless of zero multiplicity.
decisive_check.remainder_contradiction: The asserted remainder gives L(s)=L(0)-s*Delta/(s+1)+s*integral_1^infinity R(x)x^(-s-1)dx. For epsilon<1/4 this expression is holomorphic near s0, apart from possible pole-1 elsewhere, contradicting the genuine pole.
decisive_check.endpoint_robustness: Integer-only T and strict versus nonstrict summation alter only O(T^-2), so they do not resolve the contradiction.

counterevidence: No assumption of simple zeros is used.
Potential numerator and Euler-factor cancellation are explicitly excluded.
The argument works for any fixed Delta; the variable misprint in its displayed product is irrelevant.
Theorem6's limiting value1/2 is not refuted; the later preprint provides an alternative proof claim.
problems.core_dependency: At PDF p.49, Section7.3 explicitly requires E(n)=n^2 R(n)<<n^delta for arbitrarily small delta. This is precisely the failed remainder estimate in another form and is used in the principal sharp-average proof.
problems.impact_boundary: Major concerns the printed core derivation. It does not establish a false limit theorem or negate the murmurations phenomenon.

independent_acceptance_check.P1: Substituting z=4*pi*s*T/d into the fixed-order Bessel leading term gives alpha/(pi*sqrt(2)), not alpha*sqrt(2/pi), with phase (-1)^(k/2-1). Q(d)<<d^-2 and the split d<=sT versus d>sT give a uniformly summable O_k(1) remainder. Absolute convergence yields F(n!)->-B/sqrt(2), B>0; for k=2 the two asserted normalized limits differ. This proves a leading-order inconsistency without numerical inference. The qualitative order and phenomenon are not refuted.
independent_acceptance_check.P2: The Euler factor identity gives L(s)=zeta(s+2)/zeta(2s+4)*H(s), with H holomorphic for Re s>-2. At s0=(rho-4)/2 under RH, zeta(rho/2)!=0 and a vanishing H-factor would require A_p^4=p^15, impossible since A_p=1 mod p. Absolute convergence precludes product cancellation. Abel summation of the asserted O(x^-2+epsilon) remainder for epsilon<1/4 would give a holomorphic continuation through that actual pole, a contradiction. Source p.49 explicitly uses E(n)=n^2R(n)<<n^delta. Integer/strict-endpoint readings do not help.
independent_acceptance_check.P2_counterevidence: The acquired later preprint On murmurations, arXiv:2609.29631v1, p.3, explicitly identifies the same obstacle and states an unconditional alternative sharp-average proof. Its full replacement proof was not certified; the 1/2 limiting conclusion is not declared false and discovery priority is not claimed.
independent_acceptance_check.P3: Balancing X^(1/2)*T^(3/16) and Y*(PX)^(1/2)/T gives T=Y^(16/19)*P^(8/19). In the actual Theorem 1 range choose delta1=1/100, delta2=1/4, X=P prime, Y=X^(3/4). The printed cutoff is T=X^(23/24), so the normalized last term is P/T=X^(1/24), not a decaying error. Source Section 3.4 explicitly uses Proposition 3.1 for the main power saving. Corrected T=X^(20/19) gives both balanced normalized terms X^(-1/19); the second term is smaller since Y^(8/19)/(X^(1/2)*P^(11/38))<1.
